Rashi on Shabbat 50a:10:1.hebrew: ומאן תנא - דלעיל דאמר צריך לקשור, ופליג אדרבן שמעון:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:10:1.english: And who is the tanna - [The one mentioned] above who said, “[One] must tie [them],” and disagrees with Rabban Shimon.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:10:2.english: And I do not know - Ze’iri said this.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:11:1.hebrew: דטרידי - ולא יכלו לקשור מבעוד יום, והתם הוא דשרי בלא קישור, אבל בעלמא — לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:11:1.english: Because they are preoccupied - And they were not able to tie [them] while it was still day; and it is [only] there that it is permitted without tying, but in general — no.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:12:1.hebrew: מכניס מלא קופתו עפר - לכסות בו צואה ורוק, ומערה העפר בביתו לארץ, ונוטלו תמיד לכל צרכיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:12:1.english: [A person] may bring a basket full of earth - To cover excrement and spittle with it; and he pours out the earth onto the ground in his house, and takes from it continually for all his needs.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:12:2.hebrew: והוא שייחד לו קרן זוית - דהוי כמוכן ועומד לכך. אבל נתנו באמצע ביתו למדרס רגלים, הרי הוא בטל לגבי קרקעית הבית, ומוקצה ואסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:12:2.english: And that is only if he designated a corner for it - For [then] it is considered prepared and set aside for this [purpose]. But if he placed it in the middle of his house for treading underfoot, it is nullified relative to the floor of the house, and is muktzeh and forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:13:1.hebrew: כרבן שמעון - דשרי במחשבה בעלמא, שאין מעשה מוכיח שעומד לעשות צרכיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:13:1.english: In accordance with Rabban Shimon - Who permits [it] with mere thought, as there is no action proving that it is designated to attend to [one's] needs.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:14:1.hebrew: דבר מעביד מעשה - שבן מעשה הוא, שיכול לעשות בו מעשה הוכחה:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:14:1.english: That is subject to performing an action - That it is subject to an action, in that one can perform on it an action that demonstrates [its designation].

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:15:1.english: Shall we say [this is subject to a dispute among] Tannaim? - [Namely,] this [ruling] of Rav Yehuda regarding something that is not capable of [having an] action [performed on it].

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:15:2.english: [One may] clean - One rubs the utensils on Shabbat to polish them.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:15:3.hebrew: חוץ מכלי כסף בגרתקון - כמין עפר שגדל בחביות של יין, וקורין לו אלו"ם, והוא עיקר תקון כלי כסף. וגורר אותו, שהכסף רך, והוא ממחק, שהוא אב מלאכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:15:3.english: Except for silver utensils with gartekon - A kind of sediment that forms in wine barrels, and they call it alum [alum], and it is the primary [agent used for] polishing silver utensils. And it scrapes it, because silver is soft, and he [thereby] smooths [it], which is a primary category of labor.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:15:4.english: But natron and sand are permitted - For it does not scrape the silver.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:16:1.hebrew: מאי לאו - הא דתניא אסור, לאו משום דגריר ליה, אלא משום מוקצה קאסר ליה. ותנא דשרי — כגון שהכניס מלא קופתו לכך ועירה על גבי קרקע; ומאן דאסר קסבר: בעינן מעשה, וזה לא יכול:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:16:1.english: What, is it not - That which was taught, “[it is] prohibited,” is not because it scrapes [the utensil], but rather he prohibits it due to muktzeh. And the tanna who permits [it is in a case] such as where he brought in a basketful [of sand] for this [purpose] and poured it onto the ground; and the one who prohibits holds: We require an action, and with this [sand], one cannot [do so].

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:17:1.hebrew: לא דכולי עלמא - במידי דלאו בר מעשה לא בעינן מעשה, דאית להו הא דרב יהודה. וטעמא, מאן דאסר — דזימנין דגריר, ואף על גב דלא מיכוין לגרור — אסור כרבי יהודה, דאמר: דבר שאין מתכוין אסור; ומאן דשרי — כר"ש. ומיהו, גרתקון אסור, דודאי גריר, ומודה ר"ש בפסיק רישיה ולא ימות:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:17:1.english: No, everyone agrees - [that] regarding something that is not subject to an action, we do not require an action, for they accept this [statement] of Rav Yehuda. And the reason of the one who prohibits is that sometimes it scrapes [the silver], and even though he does not intend to scrape, it is prohibited, in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who said: An unintended act is prohibited. And the one who permits [holds] in accordance with Rabbi Shimon. However, gartekon is prohibited, for it definitely scrapes, and Rabbi Shimon concedes in [a case of] "cut off its head and will it not die?" [an inevitable consequence].

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:19:1.hebrew: לא יחוף בהן - בנתר וחול שערו בשבת, מפני שמשירו:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:19:1.english: One may not wash with them - With natron and sand, [one may not wash] his hair on Shabbat, because it causes it to fall out.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:1:1.hebrew: נוטל את הכיסוי - אלמא בהנך דטמן נמי קאסר לטלטולי, אלא על ידי כיסוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:1:1.english: He lifts the cover - Consequently, even with those [fleeces] in which he insulated, [the tanna] forbids moving [them], except by means of the cover.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:2:1.english: He designated them for insulation - Permanently.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:4:1.hebrew: רבינא אומר - לעולם כדקאמר רבא: אם טמן בהן מותר לטלטל, דכמאן דיחדן להכי דמו. ורבא לאו אמתניתין קאי, דמתניתין בגיזין של הפתק, דודאי עתיד להחזירן משם, ולא יחדן לכך:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:4:1.english: Ravina said - In fact, [the halakha is] as Rava said: If one insulated with them, it is permitted to move [them], for they are considered as though he designated them for this [purpose]. And Rava was not referring to our Mishnah, for our Mishnah [deals] with fleeces of a storehouse [heftek], for he will certainly return them from there, and he did not designate them for this.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:4:2.hebrew: הפתק - מערכה גדולה שעורכין ומושיבין להקצותן לסחורה, שקורין ט"ש — בין של בגדים, בין של צמר, בין של חגבים ובשר מלוח:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:4:2.english: Heftek - A large stack that they arrange and set aside to designate for merchandise, which they call tas [a pile] — whether of garments, whether of wool, or of locusts and salted meat.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:5:1.hebrew: חריות - ענפים קשים כעץ. משהוקשו שדראות של לולבין ונפלו עלין שלהן, קרי להן חריות:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:5:1.english: Palm branches [chariyot] - Branches [that are] hard like wood. Once the spines of palm fronds have hardened and their leaves have fallen off, they are called chariyot.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:5:2.english: That he harvested them - Any (gathering) [cutting] of dates is called gedirah.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:5:3.hebrew: צריך לקשר - לקשרם יחד מבעוד יום, להוכיח שלישיבה עומדים. ואם לא קשרם יחד, אסור לטלטלן למחר, דלא הוי יחוד במחשבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:5:3.english: He must tie - To tie them together while it is still day, to prove that they are designated for sitting. And if he did not tie them together, it is forbidden to move them the next day, as designation by thought [alone] is not [valid] designation.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:6:1.english: And Rav Asi said: He sits - Upon them while it is still day.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:6:2.hebrew: ואע"פ שלא חישב - עליהן לישב למחר, גלי דעתיה דלישיבה קיימי:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:6:2.english: And even though he did not have in mind - About them to sit [on them] on the morrow, he revealed his intention that they stand [designated] for sitting.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:8:1.english: Pakorin - Combed flax that is placed on a wound.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:8:2.english: With tzipa - Carded wool that is placed on a wound.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:8:3.hebrew: בזמן שצבען בשמן - גלי דעתיה דלמכה קיימי, להניחן עליה בשבת — דלאו לרפואה נינהו, אלא שלא ישרטו מלבושיו את מכתו, והוה ליה כמלבוש דעלמא. אבל לא צבען בשמן — דלאו מלבוש נינהו — הוה ליה משאוי, ואין יוצאין בו לר"ה:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:8:3.english: When he dipped them in oil - He revealed his intention that they are designated for the wound, to place them upon it on Shabbat — as they are not for healing, but rather so that his clothes will not scratch his wound, and [therefore] it is like ordinary clothing. But [if] he did not dip them in oil — since they are not [considered] clothing — it is a burden, and one may not go out with it into the public domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:8:4.hebrew: ואם יצא בהן כו' - היינו כרב אסי, דאמר: ישב, אע"פ שלא קשר ולא חישב:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:8:4.english: And if he went out with them, etc. - This is in accordance with Rav Asi, who said: [If] he sat [upon them], even though he did not tie [them] and did not designate [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:9:1.english: We too have also learned - In accordance with Rav Asi.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:9:2.hebrew: קש - סתמיה לטינא קאי, ללבנים או להסקה, ומוקצה הוא. ואם היה נתון על המטה, ולא לשכב עליו, ובא בשבת לשכב עליו, והוצרך לנענעו ולשוטחו לשכיבה, שלא יהא צבור וקשה:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:9:2.english: Straw - By default, it is designated for clay for bricks, or for fuel, and [therefore] it is muktzeh. And if it was placed on the bed, but not [with the intention] to lie upon it, and one came on Shabbat to lie upon it, and needed to move it and spread it out for lying down, so that it would not be bunched up and hard:

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:9:3.english: He may not move it with his hand - For it is forbidden to move it.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:9:4.english: But he may move it with his body - In a backhanded manner.

Rashi on Shabbat 50a:9:5.hebrew: או שהיה עליו כר או סדין - ששכב עליו מבעוד יום, ואע"פ שלא יחדו לכך ולא חישב עליו — דהיינו כרב אסי:
Rashi on Shabbat 50a:9:5.english: Or if there was a pillow or sheet over it - That he lay upon it while it was still day; and even though he did not designate it for this [purpose] and did not form an intention regarding it — which is in accordance with Rav Asi.

Tosafot on Shabbat 50a:10:1.hebrew: ולא ידענא אי בית האבל הוה - פי': אי משום בית האבל התיר, אי משום בית המשתה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 50a:10:1.english: "And I do not know if it was the house of mourning" - Explanation: Whether he permitted [it] on account of [it being] a house of mourning, or on account of [it being] a house of [a wedding] feast.

Tosafot on Shabbat 50a:2:1.hebrew: אלא אי איתמר כו' - אין גירסא זו נכונה, דלכאורה משמע שלרבא עצמו היה מקשה, וטפי הוי ניחא אי הוה גרס: "אלא אמר רבא". אבל לפי זה, הוה צריך לומר דרבינא לפלוגי אתא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 50a:2:1.english: "Rather, if it was stated," etc. - This reading is not correct, for seemingly it implies that he was raising an objection to Rava himself, and it would be more fitting if it read, "Rather, Rava said." But according to this, one would have to say that Ravina came to disagree [with Rava].

Tosafot on Shabbat 50a:4:1.hebrew: רבינא אומר בשל הפתק שנו - ומילתא דרבא כדקאמר מעיקרא, ובשאינה של הפתק. ותימה: דרבא קאמר "לא שנו", משמע דאמתניתין קאי, והא מתניתין מיירי בשל הפתק! וי"ל, דרישא מיירי בכל גיזי צמר, בין של הפתק בין שאינם של הפתק, דאין מטלטלים אותן; וקאמר רבא: "לא שנו" — בהנהו שאינה של הפתק — "אלא שלא טמן בהן, אבל טמן בהן מטלטלים אותן". והא דקתני סיפא: "כיצד הוא עושה כו'" — בשל הפתק קאמר, ואע"פ שטמן בהן אין מטלטלין, כיון שלא הזמינן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 50a:4:1.english: Ravina said: They taught regarding [wool] of a storehouse - And Rava's statement [stands] as he said initially, and [it refers] to [wool] that is not of a storehouse. And it is difficult: For Rava said "They taught [this] only...", which implies that he is referring to the Mishnah, and yet the Mishnah deals with [wool] of a storehouse! And one can say that the opening clause [of the Mishnah] deals with all wool fleeces, whether of a storehouse or not of a storehouse, [stating] that one may not move them; and Rava said: "They taught [this] only" — regarding those that are not of a storehouse — "where he did not insulate in them, but if he insulated in them, one may move them." And that which the latter clause teaches: "What should he do? etc." — it is speaking of [wool] of a storehouse, and even though he insulated in them, one may not move [them], since he did not designate them.

Tosafot on Shabbat 50a:7:1.hebrew: ורב אסי אמר ישב אע"פ שלא קשר ושלא חישב - רבינו שמשון הזקן פסק כרב אסי, מדקאמר בסמוך רב אשי, שהוא בתראה: "מתני' נמי דיקא". ור"ת פוסק כרב מכח קושיא, כמו שמפורש בפרק כל הכלים (לקמן שבת דף קכו. בד"ה ר"י אומר ושם):
Tosafot on Shabbat 50a:7:1.english: "And Rav Asi said: [If] he sat [on them], even though he did not tie [them] and did not intend [to sit on them]" - Rabbeinu Shimshon the Elder ruled in accordance with Rav Asi, since Rav Ashi, who is a later authority, stated nearby: "The mishna is also precise [in support of this]." And Rabbeinu Tam rules in accordance with Rav on account of a difficulty, as is explained in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaKelim (below, Shabbat 126a, s.v. Rabbi Yehuda omer, and there).

Tosafot on Shabbat 50a:8:1.hebrew: בפקורין ובציפא - פר"ח: כיפה שיש בה שער, ונותנין אותה בראש הקרח, ונראה שהוא שער ראשו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 50a:8:1.english: "With pakorin and with tzipa" - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: A cap that has hair, which they place on the head of a bald person, and it appears to be the hair of his head.

Tosafot on Shabbat 50a:8:2.hebrew: אבל לא צבען בשמן אין יוצאין בהן - לאו דוקא "אין יוצאין", דאפילו לטלטלם אסור, לפי שאינם מוכנים; אלא נקט "אין יוצאין" אגב רישא. ובסמוך נמי דקאמר: "אבל יצא בהן שעה אחת מבעוד יום" — לאו דוקא "יצא", דהוא הדין ישב בהן בביתו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 50a:8:2.english: "However, if he did not dip them in oil, one may not go out with them" - [The ruling] "one may not go out" is not meant precisely, for even to move them is forbidden, since they are not prepared [for use on Shabbat]; rather, [the tanna] stated "one may not go out" on account of the opening clause. And likewise, when [the baraita] states nearby: "However, if he went out with them for a brief period while it was still day" — [the expression] "he went out" is not meant precisely, for the same law applies if he [merely] sat with them in his house.

Tosafot on Shabbat 50a:8:3.hebrew: ואם יצא בהן שעה אחת כו' - אע"פ שלא צבע ולא חישב, היינו כרב אסי, דאמר: ישב, אע"פ שלא חישב ולא קישר. קשה לר"י: רישא, דקתני "יוצאין בהן בזמן שצבען", מאי אריא צבען? אפילו חישב נמי! דהא כיון דמתיר יצא אע"פ שלא צבע ולא חישב, כל שכן חישב ולא צבע, דלכאורה ישיבה גריעא ממחשבה, וכן נמי יציאה. ותירץ: דהאי דקאמר צבען — לא לצאת בהן בשבת, אלא כדי לצאת בהן מבעוד יום, ואחר כך נמלך; ואפ"ה יכול לצאת בהן בשבת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 50a:8:3.english: "And if he went out with them for a brief period, etc." - [Even though] he did not dye [them] and did not have [them] in mind — this is in accordance with Rav Asi, who said: [If he] sat [on them], even though he did not have [them] in mind and did not tie [them]. The Ri finds difficult the first clause [of the baraita], which teaches: "One may go out with them when he dyed them." Why specifically [if he] dyed them? Even [if he merely] had [them] in mind as well! For since it permits [if] he went out [with them] even though he did not dye [them] and did not have [them] in mind, all the more so [if] he had [them] in mind and did not dye [them], as ostensibly sitting [on an item] is inferior to thought, and so too going out [with it]. And he answered: That which it says "dyed them" [means] not [that he dyed them] to go out with them on Shabbat, but rather in order to go out with them while it was still day, and afterward he changed his mind; and even so, he may go out with them on Shabbat.
